text: "Turning ladies into a corporation" is how a Straits Settlements enactment, quoted in the Supreme Court this morning, strikes the Chief Justice, Sir Henry Cowper Gollan.

label: text
text:
Mr. Eldon Potter K.C., together with Mr. F. C. Jenkin, are arguing the rights under Chinese law of a fourth wife to administer the estate of her deceased husband and claim that the rights of a fourth wife or concubine as regards estate are the same as the kit fat (principal) wife.
In illustration of a point made at the court this morning Mr. Potter told His Fordship that in Singapore where the status of a concubine was not defined, the law had been faced with considerable difficulty when it came to the administration of estates. The whole of the unions of concubines or wives had to be held as polygamous or treated as the same, and it had now been decided that even if there was one kit fall and five concubines the share of the widow to the estate must be distributed among them equally. They thus got between them the widow's share which was a third of the estate.

label: text
text: "In fact, it turns the ladies into a corporation," said His-Lordship amidst laughter.

label: text
text: Mr. Potter said that by the introduction of the law it certainly appeared that a "good many camels" had been swallowed. He believed that the authorities recognised that it was straining the law with but they had had to do it.

label: text
text: His Lordship remarked that it would be an interesting body of law to observe in operation, and Mr. Potter replied that it had received the sanction of the Privy Council.

label: text
text: Regarding a very much disputed translation, Mr. Potter put into Court this morning an extract from a book of translations of Chinese law by Sir George Thomas Stainton. This stated definitely that in the case of a substituted and adopted mother of children of a deceased, she would rank equally with the natural mother and be understood to be referred to as such in all laws except in the case of violent crime being committed by her.

label: text
text: This, it is the contention of Mr. Polter, substantiates the claim of the fourth wife in the case in question to right of administration of the estate.

Contracts have been let, the "China Mail" understands, for the work of building a meteorological station equipped with wireless on Pratas Shonal. From an authentic source it is also learned that it is a stipulation of the contract that the station shall be ready for use by next October.
When the “China Mail” first published the information that the Hydrographic Department of the Chinese Admiralty had undertaken to build a station at Pratas, it was hoped that the station would be completed in time for this year's typhoon period, but the work of preliminary survey has taken longer than was anticipated. A Building Committee has been appointed, reports Dr. R. Maclean Gibson, to submit a scheme for rebuilding on the sites in Bonham Road and Breezy Path; plans are under consideration and it is expected that a public appeal will be made later. The co-operation of all interested in the relief of suffering is asked for in order that a special effort may be made to bring the hospital building up to modern requirements.
An increase in subscriptions is noted, this being attributed to the good work of the Hon. Mr. P. H. Holyoak and Mr. Chau-Siu-ki, also Mr. E. A. Harlow, Business Manager. The deficit has been reduced from $6,601 to $1,443. It had thus been possible to treat many who were unable to afford the small charge for food which was paid by in-patients. For the good work of the hospital to progress still further even greater support was needed and the Committee emphasised the advantage that new bequests would be so that a larger income could be received from interest on investments. The Hongkong Government, however, is being kept in touch with developments, as the Chinese Admiralty has made it clear since it first offered to put in hand the work itself that it would welcome the assistance of the Hongkong Government in the matter of tending the station. In this connection it is interesting to recall that a special tug is under construction for the Hongkong Government, part of the functions of which, it is thought, will be to act as a relief ship to the station on the Pratas. The tug is to be fitted with wireless, search-lights and all facilities for first aid.

label: text
text: The value of the Pratas Shoal as an observation station lies in the key position it holds in regard to the passage of typhoon and in an interview Mr. T. F. Claxton, Director of the Royal Observatory, said that the erection of a station there would mark the entrance upon a very important stage in the history of typhoon warning provisions for South China. Regular meteorological observations four times a day, say, would strengthen his hands considerably in the matter of typhoon warnings.
